limitations: Only the normalized isotropic Gaussian heat multiplier on the flat two-torus is treated.
Strict commutator-energy separation is proved at sufficiently small positive heat times, not all times.
The exhibited cost is minimal within hyperbolic determinant-one integer matrices with matching trace and squared Frobenius norm; it is not a universal spectral classification.
Classical Poisson summation and binary quadratic form methods are credited; no independent mathematical validation is asserted.
scientific_integrity.statement: Fourier-basis calculation, Gaussian Poisson transformation, exact shortest-dual-lattice enumeration, and complete bounded integer-matrix reduction support a same-model mathematical review.

title: The first lattice-sensitive Gaussian heat-commutator twins among hyperbolic toral automorphisms
